name: TAROGE-M
full_name: Taiwan Astroparticle Radiowave Observatory for Geo-synchrotron Emissions: Mount Melbourne
summary: A high-mountain Antarctic radio array observes near-horizontal ultra-high-energy air showers and tests interpretations of unusual ANITA-like events.
detection_principle: Directional antennas view the horizon for impulsive geomagnetic emission. A broad visible area, radio-quiet setting and strong local magnetic field enhance air-shower detection; timing reconstructs arrival direction.

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: The 2025 collaboration update explicitly reports two stations operating after the January upgrade.

timeline.event: Second upgrade completed; two operating stations reported.

collaboration.name: TAROGE-M Collaboration

key_parameters.name: Site
key_parameters.value: Mount Melbourne, Antarctica; approximately 2.7 km elevation

key_parameters.name: Radio band
key_parameters.value: Approximately 180–450 MHz in the founding detector description

results.summary: Initial analysis of 148 days identified about 34 UHE cosmic-ray candidates. These are air-shower candidates, not a reported neutrino discovery.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
